title: 闭着眼，怎么知道蚊子在左边？
title_en: Eyes Closed, How Do You Know the Mosquito Is on the Left?

segments.zh: 闭上眼，一只蚊子在耳边嗡嗡，
segments.en: Eyes closed, a mosquito buzzes by your ear,

segments.zh: 你一巴掌就知道往左边拍。
segments.en: and you know to slap left.
Your ears have no eyes.

segments.zh: 它怎么知道声音从哪来？
segments.en: So how do they know where a sound comes from?

segments.zh: 即将开幕的进博会上，一款人工耳蜗要来首秀，
segments.en: At the upcoming China Import Expo, a cochlear implant debuts,

segments.zh: 卖点就是：能找出声音的方向。
segments.en: and its selling point is finding where sound comes from.
It's called Integro,
and it reportedly uses AI to process sound.
Today's brain teaser:

segments.zh: 两只耳朵，怎么算出一个方向？
segments.en: how do two ears work out a direction?

segments.zh: 先看你的脑袋：两只耳朵，
segments.en: Look at your head: two ears,

segments.zh: 一左一右，中间隔着一颗头。
segments.en: one left, one right, a head in between.

segments.zh: 蚊子在左边，声音先到左耳，
segments.en: Mosquito on the left: the sound hits your left ear first,
then wraps around your head to the right.

segments.zh: 声音一秒钟走三百四十米，
segments.en: Sound travels 340 meters a second,

segments.zh: 绕过脑袋，估算大约二十厘米。
segments.en: and the trip around your head is roughly 20 centimeters.
Do the math: the two ears differ by at most
0.6 milliseconds.

segments.zh: 眨一下眼要一百多毫秒，
segments.en: A blink takes over 100 milliseconds.

segments.zh: 这个差比眨眼短几百倍。
segments.en: This gap is hundreds of times shorter.

segments.zh: 可你的大脑，最灵的时候能分出
segments.en: Yet at its best your brain can tell apart
about ten microseconds!

segments.zh: 怎么做到的？想象两个人
segments.en: How? Picture two runners

segments.zh: 从两头往中间跑着送信。
segments.en: carrying letters from both ends toward the middle.

segments.zh: 左耳的信先出发，两人就在偏右的地方碰头；
segments.en: The left letter leaves first, so they meet right of center.

segments.zh: 大脑看在哪碰头，就知道方向。
segments.en: Where they meet tells the brain the direction.
It's called the delay-line model,

segments.zh: 在猫头鹰的脑子里真找到了这样的线路。
segments.en: and barn owls really have wiring like this.
Twist one: timing alone
gets confused by high notes.

segments.zh: 高音的波很短，脑袋就像一堵墙，
segments.en: High notes have short waves, so your head acts like a wall
and casts a sound shadow.

segments.zh: 所以离得远的那只耳朵，
segments.en: So the far ear
hears it quieter.

segments.zh: 低音看时间差，高音看音量差，
segments.en: Low notes: timing. High notes: loudness.
The brain uses both.
Twist two, the weird one:

segments.zh: 正前方和正后方，时间差一模一样！
segments.en: dead ahead and dead behind give the exact same timing!
A sound in front and one behind
are equally far from both ears.
Now your outer ear takes over,

segments.zh: 就是你耳朵上那些弯弯绕绕。
segments.en: all those curls and folds.

segments.zh: 声音从不同方向进来，被弯弯绕绕弹一弹，
segments.en: Sound from each direction bounces off the folds,
and its tone quietly changes.
Your brain learned long ago:
this tone means behind you.

segments.zh: 还拿不准？你会下意识地
segments.en: Still not sure? You tilt your head
without thinking.
Tilt, and the timing changes.
Answer found.

segments.zh: 想帮人找方向的设备，也得用好几个麦克风，
segments.en: A device that helps people find direction needs several microphones
to do the same math again.
Robots do it too:

segments.zh: 扫地机、机器狗、智能音箱。
segments.en: robot vacuums, robot dogs, smart speakers.

segments.zh: 智能音箱上有一圈麦克风，
segments.en: A smart speaker has a ring of microphones,
comparing who hears it first.
The farther apart the microphones,
the sharper the direction.
Fine print: hearing the direction
is not the same as hearing clearly.
How well this implant works

segments.zh: 还要看真实使用的数据。
segments.en: still depends on real-world data.

segments.zh: 所以两只耳朵怎么算方向？
segments.en: So how do two ears find a direction?

segments.zh: 比时间、比音量、听音色、再歪个头。
segments.en: Timing, loudness, tone, and a head tilt.
A microsecond-level algorithm
running on your head all day.
Sadly, knowing the mosquito is on the left
doesn't mean you'll hit it.
It's long gone,

segments.zh: 还顺手在右边叮了一口。
segments.en: and it bit your right side on the way out.
